attempts.input: a1: Two tabs (A, B) open on one saved project 'Seed'. Both rename in the same instant (Promise.all of two fills: 'A-work-i', 'B-work-i'), so both 300 ms delayed saves fire together. Nobody closes. 15 trials.
attempts.observed: No violation. In 13/15 A said 'Saved in this browser, on this computer' with storage = A-work, and B said 'Not saving: see the notice at the top of the page' with the hold 'This project was just changed in another tab or window...'. In 2/15 (i=5, i=12) both tabs wrote and both stopped saving; in i=12 storage held B-work-12 while B's own notice said the project 'was just changed in another tab' (B's copy is the one stored; the notice still offers both choices, and no work was lost while both tabs stay open). No kept copies, no network requests.

attempts.input: a2: Two tabs; both rename in the same instant; tab A closed (page.close with runBeforeUnload) 290-340 ms later, around its own save. 30 + 12 trials.
attempts.observed: No loss in 42 trials. A always won the write (it was filled first); B stopped saving with the hold notice. In one trial (i=11, 340 ms) B won; A stopped saving and its work was kept as a copy ('A-work-11') with the kept note set.

attempts.input: a3: Tab B renames at t0; tab A renames at t0+d (d = 250..345 ms in 5 ms steps) and is closed at once, so A's leave-page write lands in the same moment that B's delayed save fires. 40 trials.
attempts.observed: No loss: 15 trials storage = A's work, B stopped saving; 25 trials storage = B's work, B 'Saved in this browser', A's work kept as a copy and the kept note set. No case where B said 'Saved' over a project storage did not hold. Note: in the 25 cases tab B (still open) says nothing about A's kept copy; the word is left only for the next opening.

attempts.input: a4 keep2: Three tabs. A renames -> B and C stop saving. B and C each rename while stopped, then 'Keep this tab’s copy' is clicked in B and C in the same instant (Promise.all). 10 trials. (Re-test of earlier finding 2.)
attempts.observed: No 'Saved' over lost work in 10 trials. Typical result: both B and C wrote; each heard the other, and all three tabs ended at 'Not saving: see the notice...'; storage = C-0, B's work only on B's screen with the hold still offering both buttons. Minor: the other tab's copy was kept twice (copies ['A-0','A-0']): both tabs kept the same copy at the same instant, so the de-duplication check did not hold across tabs.

attempts.input: a4 keepclose / keepreload: same three-tab setup; 'Keep this tab’s copy' in B in the same instant as closing C (runBeforeUnload) or reloading C. 5 trials each.
attempts.observed: No violation in 10 trials. Example (keepreload): B 'Saved', storage B-0, C after reload shows B-0, copies ['C-0','A-0']; every tab's work is stored or kept.

attempts.input: a5: Tab A renames and at once navigates to another local page (with and without waiting 400 ms); tab B renames; A presses Back; A renames again and closes at once. 4 trials.
attempts.observed: No violation. The page was not restored from the back-forward cache (fresh load). A's leave wrote A-left; B's save then hit a conflict and B stopped saving (its work stays on B's screen). A after Back showed A-left with 'Saved in this browser' (true: storage = A-left). A's next rename and close was stored (A-again). No network requests.

attempts.input: a7: Three tabs (A, B, C) on one saved project. All three rename in the same instant ('A-i','B-i','C-i'). 280-325 ms later, before or as their 300 ms saves fire, tabs A and B are closed in the same instant (page.close with runBeforeUnload, i.e. the owner closes two tabs at once). C stays open. 8 + 14 trials.
attempts.observed: WIN, 2 of 22 trials (both at the 280 ms delay, i=0 in each run; 2 of 6 trials at that delay). Final storage: stored = 'B-0', kept copies = [] (none), kept note = null. Tab A's work 'A-0' is in storage nowhere: not the saved project, not a kept copy. A gave no warning and no 'leave this page?' question, and no notice is left for the next opening. C shows 'Not saving: see the notice at the top of the page' / 'This project was just changed in another tab or window...'. C's 'Keep this tab’s copy' would keep only B-0. Cause, read from the source (apps/studio/src/platform.ts saveBrowserNow, store.ts leaveSafely): each closing tab checks that storage still holds the save it last saw, then writes. Both tabs make the check before either sees the other's write, so both pass, and the second write replaces the first without keeping a copy. Each tab then counts its work as saved and closes. The per-entry fix for kept copies (finding 1) does not cover this: these tabs were saving, so they wrote the saved project itself. The other 20 trials held: the losing tab's work was kept as a copy and the note was set.

attempts.input: a6: Tab B renames and saves 'B-saved', so tabs A and C stop saving. A and C each rename to the same text 'Same work' (identical unsaved work). A goes to the background, so the Studio keeps A's 'running copy'. C is closed for real (runBeforeUnload). A renames to 'A moved on' and goes to the background again. Then B is reloaded. Caveat: 'goes to the background' was SIMULATED (document.visibilityState overridden to 'hidden' and visibilitychange dispatched), because headless Chromium does not hide tabs; window minimising through CDP was tried and fired no event (probe-hide.cjs). The close of C is real.
attempts.observed: WIN (with the simulation caveat). After A first went to the background: copies ['Same work'], note '1'. After C closed: copies unchanged ['Same work']. C found a copy with the same text and kept none of its own. After A went to the background again: copies ['A moved on'] only. keepRunningCopy removed A's earlier running copy, the one that C's work depended on. C's work 'Same work' is now nowhere (C_WORK_LOST true). B after reload shows the notice: 'A page of the Studio closed or reloaded while it was not saving. The Studio kept that page’s unsaved work as a copy; you find it on the Summary, under “Copies the Studio kept for you”'. That statement is untrue for C: the only copy is A's later work. Cause: the de-duplication check in keepRunningCopy/leaveSafely ('a copy with this text already exists') relies on a copy that another tab owns and later removes. No network requests.
